title: Mealworms Can Eat Plastic Waste
main_content:
Styrofoam cannot be recycled without releasing dangerous pollution into the air. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency says it is the fifth-largest creator of hazardous waste.

Worms to the rescue. Specifically, mealworms.

Scientists from the U.S. and China have discovered that mealworms can digest plastic. One mealworm can digest a pill-sized amount of plastic a day.

Study co-author Wei-Min Wu says that in 24 hours, the plastic is turned into carbon dioxide.

Are the worms hurt by eating plastic? The study found that worms eating Styrofoam were as healthy as worms eating bran.

The researchers will study the worm’s eating habits.

Solving the issue of plastic pollution is important says Wu, a Stanford University environmental engineering instructor. Landfill space is becoming limited, he says.

questions.question: How much plastic can a mealworm digest in a day?
options: A mealworm can digest as much plastic as its own body weight.
One mealworm can digest a pill-sized amount of plastic a day.
A mealworm can digest multiple ounces of plastic daily.
Mealworms are capable of consuming unlimited amounts of plastic.
questions.answer: One mealworm can digest a pill-sized amount of plastic a day.

questions.question: Are mealworms hurt by eating plastic?
options: Yes, they suffer health issues due to plastic consumption.
No, the study found they are as healthy as worms eating bran.
They become lethargic and unhealthy from plastic.
Only some mealworms can digest plastic without harm.
questions.answer: No, the study found they are as healthy as worms eating bran.

questions.question: What did Wei-Min Wu say about landfills?
options: Landfills are the best way to dispose of plastic waste.
There is no concern regarding landfill usage.
